entries.definition: Concrete input demonstrating that a proof harness permits the intended state.

edition_notes.note: This laboratory abstraction is a program contract; ISO C does not enforce its lifecycle or target-specific obligations.

distinguish_from.distinction: Success can be vacuous if assumptions exclude all relevant states.

idiom: verification assumption witness requires an explicit contract.
entries.misconception: Repair wrapping arithmetic that reports success and a harness that assumes away every overflow input. Demonstrate a witness satisfying the assumptions and violating the mutant.

recall.define: Define verification assumption witness with its invariant.
recall.distinguish: Distinguish verification assumption witness from proof success.
recall.counterexample: Generalize to checked multiplication and mixed-width conversion, deriving a new precondition rather than mechanically substituting the addition predicate.

recall.distinguish: For Formal verification, falsification and fuzzing, distinguish these near concepts: verification assumption witness versus proof success; failure postcondition versus success invariant; search partition invariant versus sortedness precondition; termination variant versus iteration limit; stateful test oracle versus final-state assertion; rejection atomicity property versus atomic machine instruction; semantic fuzz oracle versus crash oracle; fuzz input reset versus process restart; one-minimal reproducer versus globally smallest input; failure-predicate preservation versus nonzero status; schedule exploration bound versus all executions; lifecycle safety invariant versus liveness; input-derived determinism versus constant output; session fuzz encoding versus accidental global history; bounded proof claim versus universal correctness; verification claim audit versus test-count report.
